name: walkthrough
title: Garbage Collection: Memory Management from First Principles
description: Walk through simulated heap, reference counting, mark-and-sweep, Cheney copying collector, and integration with Mini interpreter.

steps.description: Define Heap class for simulated memory
Define alloc that assigns address from free list
Define get and free_addr for memory management
Allocate pair and num objects

steps.question: What is the object at b?

steps.description: Move to reference counting
Define RCHeap class for reference counting
Define alloc that initializes refcount to 0
Define inc_ref to increment reference count
Define dec_ref that collects when count reaches 0
Create linked structure a -> b -> c and set refcounts

steps.question: What happens when dropping root reference to a?

steps.description: Move to cycle problem demonstration
Create new RCHeap for cycle demo
Create cycle a -> b -> a and increment refcounts
Drop roots and show cycle is not collected

steps.question: What is the final live count after dropping roots?

steps.description: Move to mark-and-sweep
Define MSHeap with memory, free_list, and roots
Define _mark with worklist for tri-color marking
Define _sweep to free unmarked objects
Create tree structure with shared node d
Run mark-and-sweep GC

steps.question: How many objects are freed by the first GC?

steps.description: Move to Cheney copying collector
Define CheneyHeap with two semi-spaces
Define alloc with bump pointer in from-space
Define _copy that leaves forwarding pointer
Define collect that copies, scans, swaps semi-spaces
Run Cheney GC

steps.question: How many live objects after GC?

steps.description: Move to integration with Mini interpreter
Define GCAwareEval with heap and environment
Define alloc_num and alloc_closure
Define get_roots to collect heap addresses from env
Test with MSHeap and evaluate 21 + 21
